speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh
text: asked	the Minister for Manpower whether the Government will allow more foreign domestic, healthcare and childcare workers into Singapore to meet the needs of an ageing population and increasing fertility rates.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: For example, there are Professional Conversion Programmes (PCPs) for occupations, such as registered nurses and pre-school teachers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: However, we also recognise that time is needed to expand our local manpower pipeline for the healthcare and childcare sectors.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: Apart from institutional care, families that need help with caring for their young children or elderly family members at home can hire foreign domestic workers (FDWs).

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: It is in the interest of employers to ensure that the FDWs they employ have the requisite skills, aptitude and supervision to perform their roles well.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: Families should consider sending their FDWs for such training so that they can provide better care for the elderly and persons with disabilities in the family.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: My question is whether there will be a near future review of the manpower needs in view of the lead time that is required and also because by 2030, that is, in another 13 years' time, in fact, one out of four Singaporeans will be aged 65 and above.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I think that is something that we always bear in mind.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: With that in mind, when will MOM review whether we would need some more manpower or whether the training programmes or the take-up rate will be sufficient to meet the demand?
